newsitem.title: UK: SmithKline up as underlying growth pleases.
newsitem.headline: SmithKline up as underlying growth pleases.

text.p: SmithKline Beecham Plc shares rose on Tuesday after the drug group's eight percent profit increase fell at the low end of forecasts, but the company said underlying growth was "excellent," dealers said.
After initially retreating in the wake of the results, the stock was up 21p at 927 by 1258 GMT -- back to its level before the figures were released -- in volume of 4.1 million shares.
"People saw the headline figure and marked the stock down," said one market-maker, "but the statement was reasonably okay and underneath they are doing very well."
SmithKline said pre-tax profit rose to 418 million stg in the first quarter from 387 million a year before, compared with expectations mostly between 420 million stg and 430 million.

Finance director Hugh Collum said underlying growth was excellent, boosted by growth in new products in pharmaceuticals and consumer healthcare, though the headline figures were hit by the strength of sterling.
Other leading drug stocks also extended early gains on the back of a firm showing by U.S. drug stocks, with Zeneca Plc up 24-1/2p at 18.64 stg and Glaxo Wellcome Plc up 12-1/2p at 11.63 stg.
"There is a bit of a stock shortage in the sector," the market maker said.
